sessions.prompt:
Add parse_qty(s) to units.py: a quantity string becomes a float ("2" becomes 2.0, "1/2" becomes 0.5). Add tests.

The plan for parse_qty has one more step: it also accepts a mixed number such as "1 1/2", which becomes 1.5. Do not do that step now; leave it for a later session.

Project rule (it applies to all later work too): a quantity must be positive: any function given a quantity of zero or less raises ValueError.

Design decision for this project: a cup is 240 ml in every conversion.

given.handoff: Session 1 added parse_qty(s) with tests. Its last step is left for later: accept a mixed number such as "1 1/2".
decisions: A quantity must be positive: a quantity of zero or less raises ValueError in any function.
A cup is 240 ml in every conversion.

sessions.prompt:
Add a Recipe class to recipe.py: Recipe(name, servings) keeps name and servings as attributes; add(name, qty, unit) adds an ingredient, and items() returns the ingredients as a list of (name, qty, unit) tuples in the order they were added. Add tests.

Project rule (it applies to all later work too): ingredient names are stored in lower case with leading and trailing spaces removed, and every function that takes an ingredient name treats it the same way.

Design decision for this project: scaled quantities are rounded to 1 decimal place.

Design decision for this project: each ingredient line of a recipe card has the form 200 g flour.

given.handoff: Session 2 added Recipe(name, servings) with add and items, with tests.
decisions: Ingredient names are stored lower case without outer spaces; every function treats names the same way.
Scaled quantities are rounded to 1 decimal place.
A recipe card ingredient line has the form 200 g flour.

sessions.prompt:
Add Recipe.remove(name) to recipe.py: it removes that ingredient. Add tests.

Change to an earlier decision (it replaces the old one): scaled quantities are rounded to the nearest 0.25, not to 1 decimal place.

Design decision for this project: adding an ingredient that is already in the recipe with the same unit adds to its quantity; with a different unit it raises ValueError and changes nothing.

Design decision for this project: Recipe.remove returns True when it removed the ingredient and False when the ingredient was not in the recipe.

decisions: Supersedes 1 decimal place: scaled quantities are rounded to the nearest 0.25.
Adding an existing ingredient with the same unit adds to its quantity; a different unit raises ValueError and changes nothing.
Recipe.remove returns True when it removed the ingredient, False when it was not there.

sessions.prompt:
Add to_ml(qty, unit) to units.py: it converts a quantity in "ml", "tsp" (5 ml), "tbsp" (15 ml) or "cup" to millilitres. Add tests.

The plan for to_ml has one more step: unit names ignore case and a trailing "s" ("Tbsps" is the same as "tbsp"). Do not do that step now; leave it for a later session.

Change to an earlier decision (it replaces the old one): a cup is 250 ml in every conversion, not 240.

given.handoff: Session 4 added to_ml(qty, unit) with tests. Its last step is left for later: unit names ignore case and a trailing "s".
decisions: Supersedes 240 ml: a cup is 250 ml in every conversion.

sessions.prompt:

Change to an earlier decision (it replaces the old one): each ingredient line of a recipe card has the form flour: 200 g, not 200 g flour.

Design decision for this project: scaling to fewer than 1 serving or to more than 10 times the recipe's servings raises ValueError.

decisions: Supersedes 200 g flour: a recipe card ingredient line has the form flour: 200 g.
